title: Migrate-to-Redwood-SDK-team-quickstart-checklist
body:
Purpose:
This document is a compact, team-facing quickstart and checklist for engineering teams migrating from self-hosted LLM endpoints or other third-party SDKs to the Redwood SDK and hosted inference. Focus is on low-friction onboarding, required guardrails (auth, telemetry, cost limits), and a minimal smoke-test path so teams can validate functionality and cost before a staged rollout.

Assumptions / target audience:
- Team already has an app using an LLM endpoint (self-hosted or another provider).
- Engineers are comfortable with a small config change and running smoke tests.
- Primary goals: preserved UX, predictable latency, and cost safety.

How to use this doc:
- Follow the sections top-to-bottom for a single-session migration.
- Use the checklist items as gating criteria for canary -> prod rollout.

Quick checklist (one-pager):
1) Create API key and sandbox project in Redwood Console.
2) Add SDK dependency and small wrapper (5–10 lines) to replace original client.
3) Configure per-route cost/latency guardrails (quota, max_tokens, rate limit).
4) Enable telemetry contract and short retention for early runs.
5) Run 10 warmup requests with debug logging.
6) Run acceptance tests (n=50 seeded prompts) and compare outputs for regressions.
7) Canary at 1% traffic for 24h with alerting on qps/latency/quality regressions.
8) Expand to 10% then 50% after post-mortem checks.
9) Full cutover and deprecate old keys.

Step-by-step (expanded)
1) Provisioning and access
- Create a sandbox org or project in Redwood Console. NOTE: keep sandbox billing and a hard monthly cap until validated.
- Generate a scoped API key for the team (restrict to project, restrict to model list when possible).
- Add the key to your secret manager (AWS Secrets Manager / GCP Secret Manager / Vault).

2) Minimal wrapper + dependency
- Add the official Redwood SDK to your service (examples below). Keep wrapper thin so rollback is trivial.
- Python pip: pip install redwood-sdk==0.9.1 (pin a patch version for the pilot)
- Node npm: npm install @redwood/inference@0.9.1 --save-exact

Sample wrapper (pseudo-Python)
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient

REDWOOD_KEY = secretlookup('REDWOOD_API_KEY')
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=REDWOOD_KEY, project='team-sandbox', default_model='redwood-alpha-1')

def generate(prompt, max_tokens=256):
    resp = client.text.generate(prompt=prompt, max_tokens=max_tokens, timeout_ms=5000)
    return resp.text
```

3) Cost & safety config (must set before sending production traffic)
- Per-call: max_tokens, temperature, stop tokens.
- Route-level: rate limit (rps), burst policy, quota (tokens/day).
- Enable token-level logging for first 48 hours to reconcile billing vs expected.
- Example Redwood route config (high-level):
  - max_tokens=256, temperature=0.2, rate_limit=10 rps, daily_token_quota=1_000_000

4) Telemetry contract (required for observability)
- Basic fields to emit: request_id, route_name, model, prompt_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, error_code
- Tag each request with experiment_id or canary_label for easy filtering.
- Send a small sample of user inputs to Redwood's eval pipeline only after consent; keep PII out.
- Telemetry snippet (Node):
```
client.on('request', (info) => {
  emitMetrics({
    request_id: info.id,
    model: info.model,
    latency_ms: info.latencyMs,
    tokens_in: info.tokensIn,
    tokens_out: info.tokensOut
  })
})
```

5) Smoke tests and acceptance
- Create a 50-prompt suite: golden outputs from the existing system + invariants (safety filters, critical phrasing).
- Run locally with SDK pointing to sandbox key.
- Measure: average latency, p95 latency, tokens per request, success rate, output diffs.
- Define acceptance thresholds (example): p95 latency < 850ms, mean tokens within ±20% of baseline, safety filters triggered <= baseline + 1%.

6) Canary plan (gating)
- Canary window: 24h at 1% traffic, monitor:
  - Errors > 0.5% -> abort and rollback
  - Latency p95 > baseline * 1.5 -> rollback
  - Cost burn rate > expected by 2x -> pause and investigate
  - Quality regressions on golden prompts -> pause and create regression ticket
- If everything passes, increase to 10% for 48h, then 50% for 48h, then full. Always keep old endpoint available as fallback for automatic routing.

Rollback options
- Immediate: flip traffic routing back to previous client/endpoint using feature flag or proxy routing layer.
- Medium: throttle traffic to Redwood SDK to 0% while keeping key active for debugging.
- Postmortem: capture request/response traces (sanitized), token counts, and a diff of outputs for the failing prompts.

Testing matrix (minimal)
- Integration: 50 golden prompts against sandbox (functional + safety)
- Load: synthetic 30s burst at 2x expected peak to validate autoscaling/batching behaviors
- Chaos: simulate 5% packet loss and see retry behavior/latency distribution
- Cost simulation: run lower-temperature batch to measure tokens-out distribution

Common pitfalls and mitigations
- Unexpected token spikes: set max_tokens and per-route quotas first.
- High variance in latency: ensure correct model variant (e.g., use lower-context model for short prompts) and enable batching-friendly settings.
- Missing telemetry: instrument early and assert presence of required telemetry fields in CI.
- PII leakage: run static prompt audits and only allow consented data to be sent to eval pipelines.

Acceptance checklist (gating to 10% traffic):
- [ ] Sandbox project provisioned and key stored in secrets manager
- [ ] SDK dependency added and wrapper deployed to staging
- [ ] Telemetry contract integrated and visible in observability console
- [ ] 50-prompt acceptance suite passed with thresholds met
- [ ] Rate limits and daily token quotas configured
- [ ] Alerts configured for errors/latency/cost
- [ ] Failover route to previous endpoint validated

Notes to reviewers / TODOs
- Decide default model family for short-text flows vs long context. (Action: Claire)
- Add a small CI step that asserts telemetry fields are present for every dev run. (Action: Ravi)
- Draft a short internal how-to for support to rotate keys and revoke quickly. (Action: Diego)
- UX team: confirm any visible change in response formatting (Action: Product)

References / links
- Redwood SDK docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk (linked for convenience)
- Eval harness: github.com/redwood-inference/evals (local test suite)
- JIRA RDW-8140: migration epic

Appendix: example acceptance prompt set (small sample)
1) "Summarize the following email in two bullet points" (short business prompt)
2) "Given this product spec, return a checklist of missing privacy controls" (safety/structure)
3) "Rephrase this chatty paragraph into a concise doc-style paragraph" (format preservation)

End of doc.
